Critics dispute both the intent framing ('grooming' vs generic web pollution) and how far the audit rates generalize: a peer-reviewed October 2025 study (Alyukov et al., HKS Misinformation Review) found Pravda-linked citations mainly on obscure, data-void prompts and at far lower rates than NewsGuard's audit.
summary: The evidence base that machine-scale propaganda is reshaping what AI systems say: chatbot audit failure rates, Wikipedia citation pollution, and confirmed training-data contamination — the site's closing argument for why this story outlives any single campaign.

caveats: NewsGuard figures are prompt-audit rates with disputed methodology generalizability. An independent peer-reviewed test with published methodology now exists: Alyukov, Makhortykh, Voronovici & Sydorova (HKS Misinformation Review, Oct 2025) found only 8% of 416 chatbot responses referenced Kremlin-linked disinformation sites (1% supporting false claims), concentrated on obscure data-void prompts — supporting an information-gap explanation over deliberate grooming. State the numbers as audit results, not population estimates.

name: What the evidence says about whether any of this works

scale.cetas: no evidence AI-enabled disinformation measurably altered any election result — the null finding spans the UK, EU, France, Taiwan and India (CETaS briefing, Sept 2024) and was extended to the US in CETaS 'Safeguarding Future Elections', Nov 2024
scale.knight: 39 of 78 catalogued election deepfakes had no deceptive intent; deceptive ones replicable without AI for a few hundred dollars
scale.meta: AI content <1% of fact-checked election misinformation in 2024; genAI gains for threat actors 'incremental'
scale.eeas: 27% of 540 FIMI incidents in 2025 involved AI TTPs, +259% year-on-year
scale.hungary: 73% of surveyed Hungarians reported encountering AI-generated content on social media; 90% considered its political use unacceptable (survey via EDMO); the AI-heavy campaign lost

effectiveness: Adoption is real and accelerating; demonstrated electoral impact is absent. The open question the site should end on: measurement frameworks capture vote-swinging, not cumulative ecosystem degradation (trust erosion, parallel-reality campaigning, LLM grooming).
summary: The honesty backbone: every effectiveness claim on the site routes through this entry, which holds the null results alongside the growth curves — mirroring the 'What this does not show' discipline of the assay-family write-ups.

name: APT crossover: Russian intrusion operations against Hungary

target.audience: Ministry of Foreign Affairs networks incl. the encrypted Protected Foreign Network (VKH)

scale.compromise: complete MFA compromise documented by September 2021: internal email and every network endpoint across 150+ sites of 90+ foreign missions, with NATO/EU 'restricted'/'confidential' documents on the VKH accessible (Direkt36); 4,000+ workstations and 930 servers affected per the leaked September 2021 internal report (444/Insight Hungary)
scale.credential_exposure_2026: 795 breaches containing government emails and associated passwords, and 97 infostealer-infected government machines, in breach databases (Bellingcat — explicitly NOT an APT intrusion; assessed as poor digital hygiene)

effectiveness: The espionage layer beneath the influence layer: a decade of documented access to Hungarian state networks by GRU-linked APT28 and SVR/FSB-linked APT29, hushed up by the then-government — essential context for why 'APT campaign' and 'influence operation' must be distinguished but shown together.
summary: Not an AI or influence operation — included because the site's credibility depends on placing the IO story against the documented intrusion story: Russia read Hungary's diplomatic traffic for years while its narratives ran in Hungarian media. UNC1151/Ghostwriter, often assumed regional, has no documented Hungary targeting.
